name: H2O
baseline: nginx 1.7.9 (HTTP/1.1 local benchmark); nginx 1.9.10 in the later EC2 static-file chart
workload: Static-content HTTP/1.1 serving of a 6-byte and a 4,096-byte response, wrk -c 500 -d 30 -t 1, scores recorded as requests/second per core, h2o/0.9.0 against nginx/1.7.9 on Ubuntu 14.04 in VMware Fusion on a MacBook Pro 15-inch Early 2013.
claimed_speedup: HTTP/1.1, 6-byte content: 75,483 vs 37,289 requests/second.core (about 2.0x, derived from page data); 4,096-byte content: 59,673 vs 43,988 (about 1.36x, derived from page data). The same page's HTTP/2 table lists h2o/0.9.0 at 272,300 and 116,022 but compares only against nghttpd and trusterd, not nginx.
hardware: Ubuntu 14.04 x86-64 in VMware Fusion 7.1.0 on OS X 10.9.5, MacBook Pro 15-inch Early 2013 (CPU model not stated); the later chart used two Amazon EC2 c3.8xlarge instances
tradeoffs: C server that can also be used as a library; HTTP/1.x, HTTP/2 and experimental HTTP/3. Smaller module and ecosystem surface than nginx; configuration is YAML.
caveats: First-party numbers from 2015 (h2o 0.9.0, nginx 1.7.9); the current docs page replaced the tables with PNG charts (h2o 1.7.0 against nginx 1.9.10 with open_file_cache on c3.8xlarge, 612-byte file, 250 clients, wrk and h2load) whose values are not in the page text, so they could not be quoted. H2O build flags and CPU model are not stated, the benchmark ran in a VM on a laptop, and the nginx config is only linked as a gist. Scores are normalised per core. An older ab -c 500 -n 100000 -k run (nginx/1.7.4 35,822 and 32,885 vs H2O 76,690 and 67,866 requests/second) appears in a fork's README. No independent third-party run was reachable (project site, Fossies and nghttp2 wiki results did not include H2O against nginx). The h2o.examp1e.net site itself was blocked, so the figures come from the repo's srcdoc source at commit 9ef1ad7 (Sep 2015); the Feb 2016 commit 05588bf replaced the tables with charts.

name: httpserver.h
workload: Hello, World! (13-byte body) served on localhost, ApacheBench with 200 concurrent clients and 100,000 requests, once with keep-alive (ab -k) and once with Connection: close.
claimed_speedup: Keep-alive: 123,907.91 vs 74,441.26 requests/sec (about 1.66x, derived from page data). Connection: close: 27,605.45 vs 15,773.47 requests/sec (about 1.75x, derived from page data). Mean time per request 1.614 ms vs 2.687 ms (keep-alive) and 7.245 ms vs 12.680 ms (close).
tradeoffs: Single-header C library, event driven and non-blocking, epoll on Linux and kqueue on BSD and macOS; no Windows support, no TLS or HTTP/2 mentioned in the README, and far fewer features than nginx.
caveats: The author states the run was only a micro-benchmark for a performance reference point and explicitly makes no statement of superiority, since httpserver.h is not a competitor or replacement for NGINX. Compiler, flags and CPU model are not stated; the nginx config shown is minimal (worker_processes 1, a return 200 location) and does not disable access logging; nginx also sent more bytes per response (about 210 vs 134 from the total-transferred lines, derived from page data) because of its headers. Hello-world workload with ab as a single-threaded client on localhost, nginx version from 2018 (1.14.0). Own benchmark with partial methodology, so tier C.
